issues.detail: The two examples are prose descriptions of what the agent does, with no concrete config files, commands with full output, or before/after diffs, so they are less demonstrative than runnable examples.

scenarios.name: migrate-eslint-flat-config-hybrid
scenarios.rationale: A covers all three rubric items (runs `npx @oxlint/migrate`, installs eslint-plugin-oxlint and spreads `oxlint.configs["flat/recommended"]` last, and runs oxlint before ESLint in the script), while B only recommends flat/recommended as a fallback, preferring `buildFromOxlintConfigFile`, and its migrate command is less precise.

scenarios.name: ts-project-config-with-plugins-and-overrides
scenarios.rationale: Both configs set categories, an explicit plugin list including typescript and react, namespaced rules, and ignorePatterns, but A's test override globs (test, spec and __tests__) are broader than B's (only .test.ts and .test.tsx), and B adds an unneeded 'import' plugin.

scenarios.name: github-actions-ci-fail-on-warnings-and-precommit
scenarios.rationale: A uses `npx oxlint --deny-warnings` in the workflow, lint-staged with a js/jsx/ts/tsx glob running plain `oxlint --fix`, and says warnings never fail the build without the flag; B has the same pieces but adds `--deny-warnings` to the hook, runs the lint through an npm script, and never says warnings don't fail the build without the flag.
